name: Battle of Thapsus
note: The accounts do not give compass directions, so the armies are drawn facing each other with Caesar on the left of the plan; his right wing is therefore at the bottom and Scipio's left wing faces it. The accounts do not say where the town, the marsh or the Optimate camp lay on the field, so they are placed on Caesar's side of the plan and the distances are only a guide. The five cohorts of the fifth legion are drawn behind Caesar's left flank; the other half of the legion, kept behind the other flank, and Caesar's left-flank archers and cavalry are not drawn. The cavalry's destruction of the fortified camp is not drawn. A tradition cited from Plutarch, that Caesar had an epileptic seizure before the lines advanced, is not drawn. Juba's allied troops are drawn beside Afranius' camp; the accounts do not say where they stood. The garrison of Thapsus is drawn at the town.

phases.title: The armies draw up facing each other
phases.text: Scipio set his legions in three lines in the centre, with cavalry and light infantry on the flanks and elephants in front of them. Caesar also used three lines, with archers and cavalry on the flanks and half of the fifth legion in reserve.
phases.quote: Scipio had drawn up his legions in three lines in the centre with his cavalry and light infantry on the flanks.

phases.title: Caesar's lines advance
phases.text: A trumpeter of the seventh legion sounded the attack. Caesar saw his right surge forward and ordered a general advance.
phases.quote: A trumpeter of the VII sounded the attack and Caesar, seeing his right surge forward, ordered a general advance.

phases.title: The archers panic the elephants on one flank
phases.text: Caesar's archers on the right flank attacked the elephants facing them. The animals panicked, turned and trampled their own men.
phases.quote: Caesar's archers on the right flank attacked the elephants opposing them, causing them to panic and turn and trample their own men.

phases.title: The elephants on the other flank charge
phases.text: The elephants on the other flank charged against Caesar's left. The five cohorts of the fifth legion, placed behind that flank, met the charge.
phases.quote: The elephants on the other flank charged against Caesar's left flank.

phases.title: The fifth legion turns the elephants back
phases.text: The legionaries stabbed their pila at the elephants' eyes and weak spots and sounded their trumpets. The beasts turned and ran towards their own lines.
phases.quote: and blasted away on their trumpets frightening the beasts, causing them to turn back and run towards their own lines.

phases.title: The elephants crash into their own right flank
phases.text: The elephants that Caesar's fifth legion had turned back ran towards their own lines and crashed into Scipio's right flank.
phases.quote: They crashed into their own right flank.

phases.title: Scipio's left breaks
phases.text: After the elephants were lost, Scipio began to lose ground. His left broke first, on the wing that faced Caesar's right.
phases.quote: Metellus Scipio started to lose ground, his left broke first

phases.title: The rest of Scipio's army follows
phases.text: The rest of Scipio's army followed his left in breaking. The legions of the centre and the right flank gave way before Caesar's advancing lines.
phases.quote: his left broke first the rest followed.

phases.title: The garrison of Thapsus sallies out
phases.text: During the battle the garrison of Thapsus sallied out and attacked Caesar's siege works. The two legions he had left to continue the siege forced it back.
phases.quote: the garrison of Thapsus sallied out, attacking Caesar's siege works

phases.title: The siege legions march south
phases.text: Having forced the garrison back, the two legions marched south to reinforce the troops fortified opposite Afranius and Juba's camp.
phases.quote: these legionaries marched south to reinforce the troops fortified opposite Afranius and Juba's camp

phases.title: Afranius' camp is overrun
phases.text: Together with the troops fortified there, the legions attacked and overran Afranius' camp. They then prepared to attack the Numidians.
phases.quote: and together they attacked and overran Afranius' camp.

phases.title: Juba's allied troops leave the site
phases.text: Before the legions could attack the Numidians, Juba's allied troops abandoned the site, and with that the battle was decided.
phases.quote: Juba's allied troops abandoned the site and the battle was decided.
